Commentary.Commentary: For Lanka, except for Dimuth Karunaratne, no other batter showed any kind of fight. Apart from him, just Chandimal managed to cross the 30-run mark and that is not what you need when you face a huge deficit. The visitors are completely on the back foot and they'll need a miracle to make a game out of this now. Can they put up a better fight or will they surrender yet again? Still around 45 overs to go in the day, this could well be the last day of the game. Join us for the reply in a bit.

Coming to what happened, most of the Kiwi bowlers were on song, except for Daryl Mitchell who bowled just the one over, every other bowler took a wicket at leat. Michael Bracewell was easily the pick with a three-fer. Matt Henry was excellent too but it was a combined effort from all the bowlers. They made really use of the conditions and landed the ball on the right spot most of the times.

A top, top display from the Kiwis and a poor one from the visitors. They have lost 6 for 55 after the Lunch break and now are in dire straits. Also, NEW ZEALAND HAVE ENFORCED THE FOLLOW-ON! So, after that poor display, the Lankans will have to come out an bat again.

New Zealand will be happy as well. They have kept it simple and not allowed many runs to score. Their discipline is key and if they continue the same way, they will believe that the wicket is just around the corner. Tim Southee and Matt Henry have been just superb and will look to do the same in the next session.

A good partnership building for Sri Lanka as they were in absolute shambles at the start of Day 3. They lost Prabath Jayasuriya and Angelo Mathews in no time and needed someone to get things back on track. Karunaratne was batting superbly from one end and Dinesh Chandimal came in to rescue as both have stitched a stand over 70. Still a long way to go but Sri Lanka will hope these two continue for a long, long period.

Hello everyone to the action of Day 3. Day 2 saw the Kiwis dominated and boss the show as Kane Williamson and Henry Nicholls notched double-centuries respectively. Quite surreal to see two in a single innings. New Zealand got a massive score and asked Sri Lanka to bat a small passage but the tourist lost two wickets. Now Sri Lanka have to show some character against quality bowling and bat without losing any wickets in the first session.
...Day 3, Session1...

Sri Lanka had a small passage to play but their batters didn't show discipline as both Oshada Fernando and Kusal Mendis gave away their wicket. Credit to New Zealand bowlers to bowl maidens after maidens which created so much pressure. Sri Lanka are behind at this stage but if the batters apply themselves, they too can go onto score a big one. It won't be easy as New Zealand are absolutely pumped up. Do join us for Day 3 at 3 am IST (9.30 pm GMT, the previous day) for all the build up. Cheers!

Dominance from New Zealand. A day they will be really proud of. It started with Kane Williamson and Henry Nicholls and for hours it remained the same as the two Kiwi players noticed respective double-centuries one after the other. It could have been a lot worse but Tim Southee declared the innings with a massive first innings score. Sri Lanka had to grind hard. They were tired and sloppy on the field which didn't help them further.
